title: A change of norm removes model growth below unit gain in two selected adult worm chemical cores
abstract: We tested how unknown synaptic signs and cell weights affect transient growth in two adult worm chemical maps. A common strongly connected core had 157 neurons. Under spectral normalization of contact counts, the exact worst-sign Euclidean growth onset was 0.725536 in adult 7 and 0.813226 in adult 8. All allowed sign matrices were stable below gain 1. A diagonal norm built from positive left and right eigenvectors contracted below gain 1 for every allowed sign choice. Its cell scale factors spanned 22706-fold and 13676-fold. Binary and capped weights changed the onsets and scale spans. The matrix bounds are established theory; the contribution is a checked anatomical benchmark and its sensitivity analysis. Two selected maps, assumed count bounds, a common time constant, extreme norm weights and no matched activity limit biological inference. Source code, selected edges, hashes, checks, curves and retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Exact model growth onsets under five weight rules and stable positive-sign witnesses in two norms. Each map uses a selected common core of 157 neurons. These are model curves, not measured activity.

citations.reason: Established diagonal stability of positive systems. We apply a Perron-vector construction, not a new stability theorem.
Source table names and common-neuron exclusion rule. No code or numerical evidence reused.
Prior campaign model study using numerical abscissae in Allen slice circuits. This work instead tests unknown signs and diagonal norms on adult worm cores.
